events.title: Agatha's Almanac - Movie Showing
events.time: 7:00 PM · Mennonite Heritage Village, 231 PTH 12N, Steinbach, MB
events.description: MHV Auxiliary presents Agatha’s Almanac Doors open 6:30 pm, coffee and refreshments served Join the MHV Auxiliary for the showing of Agatha’s Almanac, the incredible true story of 90-year-old Agatha Bock. Proceeds from the event go to the MHV Auxiliary, which supports the mission of Mennonite Heritage Village. Synopsis from Agatha’s Almanac 90-year-old Agatha forges a solitary existence on her ancestral farm, preseving heirloom seeds in her handmade universe. Without a drivers license, cell phone, running water, or even a functioning landline Agatha’s daily rituals form a vivid counterpoint to modern life. Shot by an all-female crew, the project captures the handmade materiality inherent in both the medium of film and Agatha’s tactile world. It serves as a powerful conduit for often-overlooked stories, amplifying voices and rural perspectives. Agatha’s life offers a window into the experiences of a nearly lost generation, whose value and ways of living are at risk of fading as the world rapidly changes. Tickets can be purchased online, by phone, or at the front desk.

events.title: Cat on a Hot Tin Roof
events.time: 7:30 PM · Kenmor Theatre, 130 7TH STREET, Morden, MB
events.description: In Tennessee Williams’ Pulitzer Prize-winning Cat on a Hot Tin Roof, the dysfunctional but wealthy Pollitt family gathers to celebrate aging patriarch Big Daddy’s birthday. But there is more to this gathering than a family reunion– Big Daddy is dying of cancer, and he hasn’t decided which of his sons will inherit the estate. His options include favorite son Brick, who drinks himself into oblivion in order to bear the oppressive expectations of his determined wife, Maggie, or his less-favored son Gooper, his fertile wife Mae, and their five “no-neck monster” children. While sensuous Maggie “the cat” tries to work her wiles to secure a future for them, Brick spirals deeper into despair, crippled by both physical pain and emotional loss. Lurking under every practiced interaction between the Pollitts is an ulterior motive, under every smile, a challenge, and under every statement, the specter of mendacity. For the Pollitts, the truth is as hazy as the late summer sun in Mississippi, and sometimes the only way to find it is to journey through the lies. The production staged by Candlewick Players is a strong drama with mature content the characters must face as they work through the lies in their family... as a result, the play is recommended for an more mature audience.

events.title: Rosemary Siemens - Bring Back the Hymns - Live In Concert!
events.time: 7:00 PM · PW Enns Concert Hall, 783 Mountain Ave, Winkler, Manitoba
events.description: Three generations. One stage. The hymns you grew up singing, in Winkler for one night only. BRING BACK THE HYMNS comes to the PW Enns Concert Hall on Saturday, October 17. Harvest Christian Fellowship presents a benefit concert with international violin sensation Rosemary Siemens and her family. Rosemary has performed four times at New York's Carnegie Hall and was the first violinist ever to perform in the Sistine Chapel at the Vatican since its inception in 1483. She has played in over 25 countries and 40 U.S. states, for two U.S. Presidents and Canadian Prime Ministers, and won Country Gospel Album of the Year at Canada's Gospel Music Awards. Today she leads a global movement to Bring Back the Hymns through the #1 hymn channel on YouTube, with more than 700,000 subscribers and over 200 million views in every corner of the world. This concert is that movement live and in person. Rosemary is joined by her husband, JUNO-nominated saxophonist Eli Bennett, together as the acclaimed duo SaxAndViolin, along with their young sons and Rosemary's parents. Grandparents, parents and grandchildren on one stage, playing the hymns that have been handed down through their family for generations. Expect an evening that travels from Carnegie Hall to the Vatican, from the Colosseum to the Grand Ole Opry and back home to a Manitoba church pew. Timeless hymns, inspirational classics, and the stories behind them, including how gospel music shaped Rosemary's life and continues to touch people around the world. Bring your family. Bring the people who first taught you these hymns. This is a night to sing them out loud together again. Seating is limited and this one will fill up. Get your tickets early. CONCERT DETAILS Saturday, October 17, 2026 PW Enns Concert Hall 783 Mountain Ave, Winkler, MB 7:00 PM Tickets: $40 (donations gratefully accepted) In support of Harvest Christian Fellowship For more info: 1-204-829-3069
